gate_result: GATE PREMISE IS FALSE, BUT THE CONCLUSION HOLDS — skipping for a different, stronger reason.
gate_as_stated: Skip if the timeout stub cannot carry backend identity without also shipping #159.
what_i_actually_found:
The stub CAN carry backend identity, in three lines, with no #159
work at all. Verified mechanically at main_sha:

  * ProviderAttempt (agentic.py:72-81) ALREADY declares provider_id, model and backend, each
    defaulting to "".
  * ProviderProfile (providers.py:45-55) ALREADY carries .id, .backend and .model.
  * At the timeout site (main_sha agentic.py:232-243) `prof` is in scope — the very same
    statement reads prof.engine twice.
  * The sibling "provider raised" branch ~15 lines below, and the "judge raised" branch below
    that, both populate all three from that same `prof`. The timeout branch is simply the one
    that was never updated.

So #227's stated prerequisite ("Backend identity must be recorded there (issue #159) before
any per-backend canary can be selected") overstates the dependency: recording the identity is
independent of #159 and changes no behaviour, because nothing reads those fields on the
timeout path today.
why_i_skipped_anyway:
Recording identity was never the hard part. The substantive
#221+#227 fix is D1's ratified rule, and it is a routing redesign, not a patch:

  "On a page timeout, run a 1-token functional canary against the timing-out attempt's own
   backend and model; if it passes, keep the ladder intact and continue; if it fails — or
   cannot be run at all — mark that backend degraded, drop every ladder rung (and the judge)
   using it for the rest of the document, and halt with PARTIAL_SAVE_VLM_TIMEOUT only when no
   rung remains."

Three reasons not to ship that unattended tonight:

1. THE CANARY IS THE FIX AND IT CANNOT BE VERIFIED HERE. Its whole point is to distinguish a
   wedged GPU from a healthy one — #221 measured /api/tags answering 200 in 0.03s against a
   jammed GPU. A canary can only be tested against a real backend in both states. In CI there
   is no provider at all, so anything I wrote would be exercised only through a stub, i.e. the
   one component whose correctness matters would ship unverified.
2. BOTH FAILURE MODES DESTROY OUTPUT. Halt too eagerly and a healthy document is truncated
   (#222's damage); halt too late and a 45-page document burns 3.75 hours producing nothing
   (#221's damage). There is no safe direction to be wrong in, and no way to measure which way
   I was wrong before morning.
3. IT IS A LADDER-PRUNING POLICY, not a predicate change. "Drop every rung using that backend
   for the rest of the document, halt only when no rung remains" is new state threaded through
   the per-page loop, and #227's own analysis notes the default local->cloud->gemini ladder
   probes ONE endpoint for TWO rungs (PROFILE_QWEN_CLOUD.backend is "ollama-cloud" but still
   runs through localhost:11434), so "drop rungs using that backend" has a non-obvious blast
   radius that deserves a design decision, not an overnight guess.

#227 warns that fixing #221's probe alone makes behaviour worse. The same logic applies to
shipping a canary without the trigger fix, or the trigger fix without a trustworthy canary.
what_i_did_NOT_ship_but_is_safe:
The three-line identity enrichment on the timeout stub
(provider_id / model / backend from `prof`, matching the two sibling branches) is inert — no
current reader — and unblocks the canary work. I did NOT ship it, because the ticket I was
given was #221+#227 and a prerequisite-only PR is a different ticket that nobody asked for.
Offered to the owner as a candidate small PR; it would also let #159 be narrowed.
interaction_with_E6_worth_knowing:
E6 fixed WHICH machine the probe asks, not what the
probe can detect. On a machine that runs ollama, #221's finding stands unchanged: /api/tags
answers 200 during a wedge, so the halt branch is still effectively dead there. On a machine
without a local daemon, the probe still returns False, so #227's over-broad trigger can still
truncate a document in which every page succeeded. E6 therefore did NOT arm anything new — it
strictly reduces false halts on correctly-configured deployments — but it also did not close
either #221 or #227, and neither should be read as mitigated.
recommendation:
Keep #221 and #227 open and paired. Give them a design pass (the canary's
verification strategy is the crux — how do you test a wedge detector without a wedge?), not an
implementation ticket. Consider landing the three-line stub identity enrichment first as its
own trivially-reviewable PR.
canary: N/A — no code written for E7. All findings are source reads at main_sha, cited above.
deliberately_unchanged: Everything. No branch cut, no file edited, no PR opened for E7.
blockers: #221/#227 need a design decision on how a wedge detector is verified, before implementation.
